title: Leeds beats Nottingham Forest and advances in Carabao Cup
seoTitle: Leeds Beats Forest to Advance in Carabao Cup
subtitle: A free-kick goal by Anton Stach decides the match and puts the team in the next round
excerpt: Leeds United overcame Nottingham Forest 1-0 with a free-kick goal from Anton Stach, securing qualification for the second round of the Carabao Cup.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Leeds United beat Nottingham Forest 1-0 at the City Ground, securing qualification for the second round of the Carabao Cup. The decisive goal came in the final minutes, when Anton Stach converted a free-kick that caught goalkeeper Matz Sels by surprise.

What drove the search for information about the Carabao Cup

The clash between Leeds and Forest was marked by an unexpected outcome, with Stach scoring a goal of low statistical probability. The reaction to the play boosted interest from fans and the press, who closely followed the evolution of both clubs in the competition.

How Stach's goal changed the game

Stach lined up the free-kick about 30 meters from the goal line, slightly to the left of the penalty area. Although the expected goals (xG) value was only 0.03, he hit the curve and found the near corner, beating the two-man wall and tricking Sels. The goalkeeper managed to touch the ball, but couldn't prevent it from going in.

Managers' reaction

Leeds manager Daniel Farke stated that he already expected the possibility of Stach attempting the shot and praised the confidence he has in the player. "He has surprised us several times and I trust him completely," said the coach.

Oliver Glasner, recently appointed by Nottingham Forest, emphasized that the defeat will not erase the optimism brought by his appointment. He highlighted the need for stability and reinforcements, pointing out that the club is working on two or three signings to improve the squad.

Impact on the rest of the Carabao Cup

With the victory, Leeds advances to the next Carabao Cup match, which will be played once again at the City Ground against the same opponent. The result keeps Leeds' hopes alive of turning tight matches into victories, reinforcing the strategy of relying on players like Stach and James Trafford.

Future challenges for Forest

Forest, which has not yet made any signings for the new season, is looking to strengthen the team, especially in attacking positions. Glasner mentioned the intention to acquire players who bring quality and energy, citing interest in Lucas Bergvall, although no deal has been closed yet.

With information from BBC, The New York Times.
